differences: The new muzzle gives the three-quarter face more character, but it reads as a separate large cream ball hanging from the face in profile. Its underside is too round and deep, and the root transition remains visible.
The nose and lower mask now ride on top of that protruding ball. This resembles a bear/dog muzzle more than the reference's short integrated otter cheeks.
The shortened body silhouette is cleaner after removing the flank fur tabs. A long sharp cheek point still interrupts the otherwise soft head contour.
Motion was not rescored because this checkpoint changes face geometry only; the round-three motion findings still apply.
suggestions: Accept the proposed rearward shift and depth reduction: moving the muzzle center back about .008 m and reducing depth .052 to about .035 m is appropriate. Also reduce its vertical radius from .044 toward .032–.035 m and raise its center slightly, so the underside tucks into the face instead of forming a hanging ball.
Preserve most of the lateral cheek width. The desired shape is broad and shallow with two subtle cheek bulges around the nose, not another globally shrunken sphere.

Blend or union the muzzle root into the head surface with a short smooth transition. The current source contains an intersecting Muzzle mesh and Head mesh, which leaves a visible attached-ball boundary; joining objects alone will not remove that crease.

Move the smile upward with the reduced muzzle and shorten its span modestly; keep the nose seated near the upper middle of the compact pad. Refit the mask nose pocket to the final surface after that adjustment.
Shorten the isolated cheek spike and round its tip into a shallow backward-flowing clump.
reasoning: The muzzle now has useful volume, but its depth and separate-ball transition overshoot the reference. A shallower, vertically smaller pad with a smoothly integrated root should preserve the improved expression while removing the bulbous side profile.
